rationale: C17 is a strong, concrete drafting precedent. Both memoranda veto bills directing the Secretary of the Army to reconvey federally acquired interests associated with specified reservoir projects to former owners; both scrutinize an original-purchase-price mechanism, explain why the proposed administrative machinery is defective, invoke previously approved reconveyance legislation for the Demopolis project as the preferable model, and invite Congress to enact a revised bill along those lines. These similarities are far more specific than a shared veto-message format or general land policy. C09 and C19 have weaker parallels involving rejection of project-specific departures from established policy and endorsement of alternative corrective legislation, but neither shares the child's distinctive reservoir-land reconveyance machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: authorize and direct the Secretary of the Army ... to convey such interests to the former owners thereof or to their legal heirs
shared_material.parent_excerpt: authorize the Secretary of the Army ... by reconveyance of certain lands to former owners
shared_material.explanation: Both bills use the same core administrative mechanism: Army-controlled reconveyance of reservoir-project lands or interests to former owners.

shared_material.child_excerpt: upon payment to the United States of an amount equal to but not in excess of the purchase price for which said interests were acquired
shared_material.parent_excerpt: reconveyance of lands or interests in lands to former owners at what the Secretary determines to be the original purchase price
shared_material.explanation: The memoranda address materially parallel original-purchase-price provisions, with the child adapting the issue specifically to mineral interests.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I approved H. R. 7097 ... which provides for the reconveyance ... within the Demopolis Lock and Dam project, Alabama
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have approved legislation authorizing similar adjustments by reconveyance ... at Demopolis Lock and Dam, Alabama
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same previously approved Demopolis reconveyance legislation as the favorable comparison.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the job of administering this legislation would be confusing and unsatisfactory to all concerned
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This provision would unjustly expose the Secretary to a series of burdensome and time-consuming administrative proceedings
shared_material.explanation: Each veto rests substantially on the impractical administrative burden created by the bill's decision criteria.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am hopeful that the Congress may yet enact legislation ... similar to H. R. 7097
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I recommend that the Congress reconsider H.R. 7195 and enact a bill along those lines
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by requesting revised legislation modeled on the acceptable reservoir-reconveyance approach.
